import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Fill empty 'Sleep Disorder' values with 'None' for better categorization
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Set up the matplotlib figure and a single subplot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep,
# with additional insights from BMI Category, Stress Level, and Sleep Disorder.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',      # Color points based on Sleep Disorder
    style='BMI Category',      # Use different markers for BMI Category
    size='Stress Level',       # Scale marker size based on Stress Level
    sizes=(100, 800),          # Define the range of marker sizes
    alpha=0.8,                 # Set transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    palette='viridis'          # Choose a color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Sleep Disorder, BMI, and Stress Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement
plt.legend(title='Legend', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Ensure all elements fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot as output.png
plt.savefig('output.png')
